Program.cs, IServiceCollectionExtensions.cs, and WebApplicationExtensions.cs must live at the project root.

What The Standard says

“Configuration Models” — The Standard treats the entry point, dependency registration and application-routing setup as configuration models used at system launch. Keeping the three application composition files at the project root makes that exceptional role visible. read it here.

Why it matters

These files are composition entry points for the application rather than members of a business layer. Keeping them at the project root makes startup discoverable and prevents folder placement rules intended for Standard elements from disguising the application's executable boundary.

Bad code example

// Violates STXAPP001: Program.cs, IServiceCollectionExtensions.cs, and WebApplicationExtensions.cs must live at the project root.
// Services/Startup/IServiceCollectionExtensions.cs
public static class IServiceCollectionExtensions { }

Good code example

// Follows STXAPP001
// IServiceCollectionExtensions.cs (project root)
public static class IServiceCollectionExtensions { }
